limitations: Agents sharing this machine and user can read local files, so sealing detects changes after commitment but cannot stop a loop that reads an unprotected reveal. Keep the reveal away from the loop until the candidate is frozen.
Training overlap relies on the training keys a candidate declares, so undeclared training data is not detected.
The goal domain is 4-bit functions of two inputs from short programs. It measures this domain only and says nothing about general intelligence.
Retention is supplied by the caller and must be independently reproduced by the reviewer.
Thresholds are preregistered judgement calls, not derived from a power analysis.
CPU measured in-process can undercount work a candidate does in other processes, and a candidate's reported candidate count is only range-checked, so real runs need independent process metering.
Very cheap runs are dominated by timer noise and may fail the CPU gate; this errs toward NO_IMPROVEMENT, so experiments need measurable CPU per seed.
No improvement loop has used this scoreboard yet, so it has only been exercised on controls.
Controls use public seeds so reviewers can reproduce them; a real run uses new_commitment().
